extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners, researchers, policymakers, USPTO staff, and other users of PTAB AIA trial statistics
extracted.subtask_description: Methodology and definitional guidance for preparing and interpreting PTAB AIA-trial statistical outputs (by-petition, by-patent, and by-claim) including institution rates, outcome categories, claim-level categorizations, and handling of rehearings, joinders, and motions to amend.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcomes (terminations/dispositions) categories
rubrics_metrics.description: “Outcomes” are defined as the names of events that end an AIA proceeding. The outcomes consist of: FWD, Settled, Dismissed, RAJ, and Denied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pending cases are excluded. Joined cases mirror the outcome of the case to which they are joined and are excluded to avoid double counting. An RAJ may be requested by either the petitioner or the patent owner. Results of rehearings within the FY are considered in some outcome graphics (see rehearing guidance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Final Written Decision (FWD) categorization
rubrics_metrics.description: FWDs are broken into three categories: 'FWD All Patentable' (all claims addressed in the FWD were found patentable), 'FWD Mixed' (at least one claim patentable and at least one claim unpatentable), and 'FWD All Unpatentable' (all claims addressed in the FWD were found unpatentable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims originally challenged but not before PTAB in the FWD (e.g., disclaimed, canceled, or otherwise withdrawn from the proceeding) do not factor into the categorization. The FWD categorization represents PTAB’s ruling on the claim based on the evidence presented and evaluated in the FWD.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institution rate by petition (calculation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Institution rate for each fiscal year by petition is calculated by dividing petitions instituted by decisions on institution (i.e., petitions instituted plus petitions denied).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Outcomes of decisions on institution responsive to requests for rehearing are excluded for the by-petition institution-rate calculation. Institution rates by petition consider joinders but do not consider rehearing outcomes. Pending cases are excluded because they have no decision on institution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institution rate by patent (calculation)
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent is 'instituted' if any petition challenging that patent is instituted; a patent is 'denied' if no petitions challenging that patent are instituted. Institution rates by patent for a given year are the institution rates for those patents as of the end of the reported fiscal year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patents that have not received a Decision on Institution are not included. Institution rates by patent consider joinders and rehearing outcomes; rehearing outcomes are considered in the year they occur. Because of this methodology, reported institutions by patent are slightly higher than by petition; mathematically, institution rate by patent must always be higher than by petition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of rehearing outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Rehearing outcomes are handled differently depending on the metric: institution rates by petition exclude rehearing outcomes, while institution rates by patent and some outcome graphics consider rehearing outcomes in the year they occur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example rules: If a case is initially denied in FY19 but instituted on rehearing in FY20, it is counted as denied in FY19 for by-petition charts that exclude rehearing, but rehearing outcomes occurring in the subject FY are considered in the 'outcomes in FY' graphics. This difference can cause slight variances between institution-rate charts and outcome charts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent outcome aggregation rules (by patent)
rubrics_metrics.description: To determine a net outcome for a patent in a FY, identify each patent that had a petition reach an outcome in the FY and consider the outcomes of all petitions ever challenging that patent as of the end of the FY.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If there is one petition or every petition had the same outcome, that is the patent outcome. If any petition had a FWD outcome, the patent outcome is FWD (even if the FWD happened in an earlier FY). If multiple petitions have a mixture of different outcome types (and none are FWD), the patent outcome is 'mixed outcomes'. For FWD categorization by patent, the net claim outcome of all claims challenged in all FWDs addressing that patent is considered; if a claim is ever found unpatentable, the claim is listed as unpatentable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim outcome categories (by claim)
rubrics_metrics.description: For each claim of patents that reached an outcome in the FY, each claim is categorized as: denied, dismissed, found unpatentable, found patentable, disclaimed, or Challenged But No FWD.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definitions: 'Unpatentable' and 'patentable' mean PTAB found the claim unpatentable or patentable in a FWD on the merits under 35 U.S.C. 318(a). 'Disclaimed' means the patent owner requested adverse judgment on, disclaimed, or otherwise canceled the claim (often called 'RAJ'). A claim was 'denied' if it was denied in every ground of every petition challenging the claim. A claim was 'dismissed' if it was dismissed in every petition challenging the claim. 'Challenged But No FWD' covers claims challenged but not falling into the above categories (e.g., saw both a denial and a dismissal, or the underlying cases settled). If a claim saw multiple outcomes, precedence rules apply (see claim outcome precedence). The outcome reported for a given claim is assigned to one and only one category.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim outcome precedence
rubrics_metrics.description: If a claim saw multiple outcomes across proceedings, precedence is used to assign it to a single category.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Precedence used: unpatentable > disclaimed > patentable. Examples: if a claim has been found unpatentable and patentable in two different proceedings, the claim is listed as unpatentable. If a patent owner expressly cancels a claim in a motion to amend, that is categorized as a 'disclaimer.' If a patent owner merely moves to amend a claim, that is not considered a cancellation/disclaimer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion of MTA (motions to amend) proposed claims from claim statistics
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims proposed in motions to amend (MTA) are not considered in the claim-by-claim outcome reporting because MTA claims are new claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If MTA claim 31 is proposed to substitute for issued and challenged claim 1, only the results of claim 1 are reported, regardless of what happens to MTA claim 31. Refer to PTAB's MTA statistics presentations for outcomes of proposed claims in MTAs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of joined cases
rubrics_metrics.description: Joined cases mirror the outcome of the case to which they are joined and are excluded from many charts to avoid double counting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Joinders do not affect a patent's institution status, only which year(s) a patent is listed as having an institution. Example: a petition grant in FY19 and then a joinder grant to the earlier petition in FY20 would result in the patent being listed as an institution in both FYs under patent-level methodology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion of pending cases
rubrics_metrics.description: Pending cases (those that have not reached an outcome or Decision on Institution) are excluded from the presented outcome and institution-rate statistics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because pending cases have no outcome or Decision on Institution, they are by definition excluded from the FY outcome graphics and institution-rate calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of common acronyms and included proceeding types
rubrics_metrics.description: Common acronyms used: Decision on Institution (DI); Final Written Decision (FWD); Request for Adverse Judgment (RAJ); Fiscal Year (FY). The dataset includes inter partes reviews (IPR), covered business method reviews (CBM), and post grant reviews (PGR). Derivations were not considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The dataset includes the status of all petitions, patents, and claims as of the last date reported on the slide (e.g., FY20 datasets display outcomes as of close of business on 9/30/2020).

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeframe and netting rule for inclusion in FY charts
rubrics_metrics.description: Each slide reports net outcomes for petitions/patents/claims as of the end of the FY reported; outcomes occurring after the end of the FY are not considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because patent-level outcomes look at net outcomes as of the end of the FY, a patent's listed outcome for a FY may reflect events that occurred in prior FYs (for example, an earlier FWD can make a later-denied petition still count as an FWD patent outcome in the later FY).

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim Outcomes slide: No DI and No FWD categories
rubrics_metrics.description: The Claim Outcomes slide includes special categories: 'No DI' for claims that were never addressed in a Decision on Institution and 'No FWD' for claims that were instituted but never addressed in a Final Written Decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 'No DI' examples include claims not addressed due to settlement, dismissal, or petitioner's RAJ. 'No FWD' examples include claims instituted but not reaching a FWD due to settlement, dismissal, or petitioner's RAJ. The slide also explicitly shows how many claims were disclaimed pre- or post-institution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rounding conventions for percentages
rubrics_metrics.description: Percentages are rounded according to traditional convention: inspect the digit to be rounded off and if between 0 and 4 round down, if between 5 and 9 round up.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because of rounding, percentages may not always add up exactly to 100%. If numbers are rounded to add up to 100%, the convention is followed where the number closest to being rounded is rounded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visualization scaling rules (circles)
rubrics_metrics.description: The area of each circle in the circles graphic is scaled to the number of patents in the category.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 'All Patents, Fiscal Year 2020' graphic uses an estimate of 3.8 million unexpired patents obtained by starting with all patents issued and projecting expiration dates based on grant date, continuity data, maintenance fees, and patent term adjustment. Data not available (terminal disclaimers, district court invalidity findings, USPTO invalidity findings) were not accounted for but are not large enough to change three significant digits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motion to Amend (MTA) study reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Appendix A (Motion to Amend Study) presents statistics on motions to amend in AIA trials, including number of MTAs filed, dispositions, and reasons for denying entry of substitute claims (including statutory reasons).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appendix A is a separate installment; the presentation notes that Graph IV lists 'Reasons for denying entry of substitute claims' broken out into 'All reasons' and 'Statutory reasons.' For detailed MTA outcomes and the reasons for denial, refer to the MTA statistics presentations (Installment 6 through March 31, 2020).
